why: Deletions a reviewer has judged superseded, keyed by the deleted path.
`node local/sync/post-sync.mjs` inventories the exported surface of every deleted fork-only module
and fails when an export has no surviving reference. That is the right default: a module disappearing
is exactly when a caller can leave with it. This file is how a reviewed supersession is recorded so
the check can pass without weakening it.
Each entry must name the live replacement and the evidence for calling it a superset — the check
prints this, so the next sync inherits the reasoning instead of re-deriving it.
An entry whose path is no longer deleted is reported as stale, so this file cannot rot unnoticed.
Entries are therefore per sync: a previous sync's acknowledgements are pruned once their deletion is
no longer part of the tip..HEAD range.

src/main/claude/claude-turn-row-revision.reason: Upstream moved it, it was not ours to lose: `c0b07d3a71` renames `claude-turn-row-revision.ts` to the provider-neutral `agent-journal-turn-row-revision.ts` (`R068`) and updates both callers in the same commit. The four exports renamed with it — `ClaudeTurnRowTarget`/`ClaudeTurnRowWrite`/`ClaudeTurnRowDelivery` become `AgentJournalTurnRowTarget`/`AgentJournalTurnRowWrite`/`AgentJournalTurnRowDelivery` and `writeClaudeTurnRow` becomes `writeAgentJournalTurnRow`. The live tree references them from `claude-context-facts.ts` and `claude-open-turn.ts` (the same two callers the scan reported as its old referrers) plus `provider-timeline-settlement.ts` and `provider-timeline-turn-decisions.ts`, so no call was dropped in the merge. The fork never modified the file: `git diff 6c693edf40 ed0be2085f` on it and on both callers is empty, which is why the merge took upstream's move cleanly.
